newsitem.title: UK: UK says to radically overhaul agriculture ministry.
newsitem.headline: UK says to radically overhaul agriculture ministry.

text.p: British Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham said on Thursday that his ministry would be radically overhauled in the wake of scandals over mad cow disease and food poisoning.
"This department, I hope, will be changed beyond all recognition in a period of months from now," he told BBC television news in an interview.

He said a new Food Standards Agency would take responsibility for the safety of British food, ending the monopoly of the much-criticised Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAFF) over the country's food industry.
Public confidence in food has been shaken by an outbreak of E.coli food poisoning that killed 20 people and by fears that Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy, or mad cow disease, can spread to humans.
Critics say MAFF -- in charge of both promoting the food industry as well as ensuring food safety -- has been too susceptible to lobbyists for farmers and sections of the powerful industry.
"This has been a closed, inward-looking, secretive, unresponsive department which has not enjoyed the best of reputations in the last two or three years," Cunningham said.
The BBC said the new Food Standards Agency would be responsible to the health minister and parliament but would be able to enforce food safety locally without asking permission if it saw fit.
In the run-up to its landslide May 1 election win, the Labour party regularly attacked the Conservative administration for bungling the issue of food safety and promised big changes if it won.

"We have changed the priorities of the department. We have put consumers at the top of our list of priorities," Cunningham said. "These really are fundamental and far-reaching changes in the whole culture of MAFF."
